tldr: Agent-memory research started with structured retrieval: ActionRAG (Oct 23) used graph diffusion for relation-consistent evidence, and ETAMem (Oct 27) separated and aligned heterogeneous memory types. Early November papers turned to consistency, task-conditioned utility and exploration-task benchmarks.
whats_new: A Nov 9 Show HN project, MemSeal, pitches provenance containment for agent long-term memory, a trust angle the research papers in this thread had not yet covered.
why_it_matters: Memory work now spans retrieval, consistency, utility and, with MemSeal, provenance: where a stored memory came from and what it may influence. A production memory layer needs tests for each, and the new item is a project announcement, not a reviewed result.

status.detail: Work has moved from retrieval design to consistency, utility and benchmarks, and now a provenance-focused open-source project; the research items are unreplicated arXiv preprints.

beats.headline: ActionRAG and ETAMem restructure how memory is retrieved
beats.summary: Relation-aware evidence retrieval and separated memory types for long-running agents.

beats.headline: Consistency and utility become the questions
beats.summary: One paper revises dependent memories when an upstream fact changes; another measures utility per task.

beats.headline: A benchmark for memory in exploration tasks
beats.summary: Graph-based benchmark and framework for long trial-and-error work such as research and software development.

beats.headline: MemSeal frames memory as a provenance problem
beats.summary: A Show HN project on provenance containment for agent long-term memory.

open_questions: Do ActionRAG or ETAMem release code and benchmark numbers others can reproduce?
Does the dependency-aware revision method hold up on an independent long-horizon agent benchmark?
Will other memory systems report results on the new exploration-task benchmark?
Does task-conditioned utility change which memories a production agent chooses to store?
Does MemSeal publish evaluations or a threat model showing what its provenance containment actually blocks?
take_for_builders: Replay your own long-running agent traces against a plain retrieval baseline, test that changing an upstream fact updates dependent memories, and record where each memory came from; treat the papers as unreplicated preprints and MemSeal as unevaluated until it publishes results.

day_captions.db79b7b839ad79f4: Relation-aware evidence retrieval via graph diffusion for consistent answers from long histories.
day_captions.caaf392509c9e434: Separates memory types and aligns them to address entangled information in conversational memory.
day_captions.fd965980a6846281: Targets stale dependent memories when an upstream fact changes.
day_captions.9cfa80c5232a7be3: Measures memory value per downstream task instead of a single importance score.
day_captions.fb3e45410f2c29fc: Adds a graph-based benchmark and framework for memory in long exploration tasks.
day_captions.c02384b58f1bad50: Adds a provenance-containment project for agent long-term memory, the first non-paper item in the thread.
